title: Console Walkthrough - Usage Analytics & Cost Breakdown (Arcadia Retail)
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns. Arcadia asked about multi-tenant cost allocation, per-route SLOs, and hosted vs dedicated cost tradeoffs. Action items: send pricing sheet, security docs, schedule POC benchmark, prepare per-route sample dashboard for their team.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining - Maya from Redwood here, Jordan my SE is with me. Uh quick intro then we'll jump into the console.
[00:08] Samira Khan: Hi Maya, Samira here, thanks. We got Liam and Priya on from platform and finops.
[00:12] Liam O'Neill: Hey all.
[00:14] Priya Desai: Hi.
[00:16] Jordan Patel: Hey team, I'll take the demo controls in a sec. Quick note we've also shared the deck and the cost spreadsheet link, here's the link in chat: https://redwood.ai/deck/console-walkthrough
[00:28] Maya Chen: Cool, so agenda: quick setup + telemetry, then per-route dashboards, usage analytics and cost breakdowns, then Q&A and next steps - should be about 40 minutes.
[00:36] Priya Desai: That works. we're particularly interested in per-route cost allocations and how we can map tokens back to our feature teams.
[00:44] Jordan Patel: Great, that's exactly the use case we built the per-route views for. I'm going to share screen - bear with me.
[00:50] [screen share starts]
[00:54] Jordan Patel: Alright, this is the Redwood Console home. On the left you'll see routes - per-route configs. We'll open Arcadia-customer-chat route as an example, you can see throughput, tail latency and cost lines over time.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Note - the cost numbers are broken down into token processing (model cost), infra (GPU time) and platform (Redwood fee) so you can map to your FinOps buckets.
[01:22] Priya Desai: How granular is infra attribution? can we do tenant-level or business-unit?
[01:27] Jordan Patel: Yes - you can tag requests with customerTeam or project_id headers, and the console will roll up cost by tag. We'll export CSVs for chargeback. There's also an API to pull usage-by-tag nightly.
[01:40] Samira Khan: Is that per model variant? we have a few models (gpt-like open weights) and want to see which models drive the cost.
[01:47] Jordan Patel: Yep - the per-route view includes model variant breakdown, quantization status, and average tokens per request. You can filter to view only hosted vs dedicated variants.
[01:56] Liam O'Neill: Quick question on accuracy - does it use estimated tokenization or exact tokens billed?
[02:02] Maya Chen: We use the same tokenization as part of the runtime accounting - it aligns with billing. Sometimes transcript mismatch occurs but it's usually within rounding.
[02:12] [00:02:30] Maya Chen: (ah small delay) you might see small differences if you have proxy caching or external batching.
[02:20] Priya Desai: Ok, can we see an example cost breakdown for a month?
[02:24] Jordan Patel: Sure let me switch to the analytics tab - here's a 30-day view. You can see total token count, effective tokens (after caching), modeled infra-hours and per-token unit cost. The chart on the right shows top 10 routes by cost.
[02:42] Jordan Patel: You'll also notice a heatmap for sequence length distribution - that helps find where long contexts spike our infra usage.
[02:49] Samira Khan: That heatmap is useful. can we alert on shifts in distribution?
[02:52] Jordan Patel: Yes, you can create regression alerts - we have preset thresholds and can tie them to quality regressions or cost anomalies.
[02:58] [00:03:30] Liam O'Neill: For our SLOs, we want per-route p95 latency under 200ms, what knobs do we have?
[03:06] Jordan Patel: You can set per-route SLOs and the smart router will route requests to dedicated pools or faster variants if latency breaches. There's also an autoscale/burst config for Dedicated pools.
[03:15] Maya Chen: And you can specify fallback policies - e.g., if the main model isn't available, route to a cheaper quantized variant or to hosted fallback with slightly higher latency.
[03:24] Priya Desai: How is privacy handled for hosted vs dedicated? we need data isolation for PII.
[03:29] Jordan Patel: Hosted maintains tenant separation logically; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and optional VPC peering. For strict isolation you can use Private deployment. We also support KMS for key management - we integrate with customer KMS/HSM.
[03:44] Samira Khan: SOC2? audit logs?
[03:46] Maya Chen: Yes, SOC 2 Type II, ISO is available, and detailed audit logs are in the Console - you can export them and we support SAML SSO, RBAC roles too.
[03:56] [00:04:30] Priya Desai: Cost question: we run a mix of text gen for chat and batch embeddings for search re-rank. how do you combine those in the cost view?
[04:04] Jordan Patel: Different categories - we tag embeddings and generation routes separately. The console has a cross-workload view so you can compare embeddings token-equivalent cost and real-time chat token costs, plus per-request CPU/GPU usage.
[04:17] Liam O'Neill: Are embeddings billed differently?
[04:20] Maya Chen: It's still per-token or per-embedding unit depending on model, we show normalized unit costs so you can compare apples-to-apples.
[04:27] [00:05:00] Jordan Patel: I'm going to drill into a single high-cost route - you can see request histogram, median latency, p95 and the cost composition. There's also sample payloads so you can see which prompts drive long contexts.
[04:40] Samira Khan: That sample payload view is great; sometimes engineering accidentally leaves debug logs in requests which blow up token count.
[04:48] Jordan Patel: Exactly - we surface outliers and sample requests so you can add rules to strip or truncate certain fields client-side.
[04:56] Priya Desai: On chargeback: can we map costs to our internal SKUs and export to our billing system?
[05:02] Jordan Patel: Yep CSV export and webhook-based exports. You can also connect to BigQuery/S3 export for nightly ingestion.
[05:10] [00:06:00] Liam O'Neill: Let's talk about batching and caching - we want to reduce unit-cost without impacting p95.
[05:17] Jordan Patel: Redwood Optimize recommendations are surfaced in the console - it will suggest batching windows, KV cache prefixes for repeated prompts, and quantization levels per-route. You can apply suggestions as experiments and roll back if quality regressions are detected.
[05:31] Maya Chen: We do recommend running a small benchmark to validate quality vs cost - we can run a POC where we try a few quantization profiles and show delta in cost and request quality.
[05:42] Priya Desai: That would be helpful. can you run one against our 10k prompts?
[05:46] Jordan Patel: Yes - we'd want a sample set and a test harness. We can run in hosted or on a Dedicated pool to get realistic infra numbers.
[05:55] [00:07:30] Samira Khan: On networking, if we use VPC peering for Dedicated, does any data leave our VPC to Redwood control plane?
[06:01] Jordan Patel: Control plane traffic goes over the management channel - for Private you can run a fully customer-managed control plane. For Dedicated with VPC peering, inference payloads stay in peered network, but metadata and metrics may be sent back for observability unless you opt into restricted telemetry.
[06:17] Maya Chen: We can provide a diagram in the security pack. We'll note this for the security docs link in the follow up.
[06:22] [00:07:50] Liam O'Neill: Any obvious gotchas migrating from our current provider? we use some Vertex and in-house models.
[06:29] Jordan Patel: Model format conversion is usually straightforward; we support ONNX/Torch/ggml artifacts. For stateful chat we support KV cache migration patterns. We do recommend a staged rollout and traffic split so you can compare p95 and cost side-by-side.
[06:44] Priya Desai: If we pin models per route, can we do canary rollouts?
[06:48] Maya Chen: Yes, per-route rollouts: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies.
[06:53] [00:08:30] Jordan Patel: Back to analytics, here's a sample per-team report - it groups by tag and shows cost per 1k requests and cost per 1k tokens. You can apply a rate-limiting policy per-route if needed.
[07:05] Samira Khan: That's good. For FinOps we mostly need monthly CSV and an automated report - will we get that via API?
[07:11] Jordan Patel: Absolutely, nightly export or webhook push to your billing system.
[07:16] Priya Desai: Ok, switching gear - on compliance, do you have pen test reports?
[07:20] Maya Chen: Yes, pen test report and SOC2 artifact included in the security pack. We'll share SSO configuration guide too.
[07:26] [00:09:00] Liam O'Neill: Let's cover pricing high-level - what are the levers for reducing cost?
[07:31] Maya Chen: Primary levers: choose cheaper model variant for non-critical routes (quantized weights), use caching to reduce repeated prefixes, use batching for throughput workloads, and route to Dedicated vs hosted based on unit economics. We'll share an example SKU/pricing sheet.
[07:45] Priya Desai: Can you show an example of unit economics for a route?
[07:48] Jordan Patel: Sure - here's a route breakdown table: avg tokens 420, cache hit 12%, model cost $0.0012/token, infra amortized $0.0006/token, platform fee $0.0003/token => total $0.0021/token. You can toggle quantize to see drop to $0.0015/token.
[08:07] Samira Khan: Nice, that math helps.
[08:10] Maya Chen: We generally show three scenarios: baseline, optimized (caching/batching), and dedicated (reserved infra) - each with projected monthly cost.
[08:18] [00:09:50] Priya Desai: If we sign a committed Dedicated contract, how quickly can we spin up capacity?
[08:24] Jordan Patel: Typical lead times 2-6 weeks depending on region and capacity availability. We also offer burst capacity on top of committed.
[08:32] Liam O'Neill: Can we run a pilot on our VPC?
[08:35] Maya Chen: Yes, we can do a VPC peering pilot or Private deployment for a short-term POC. We'll discuss options in follow-up.
[08:42] [00:10:30] Samira Khan: Any questions from your end?
[08:34] Priya Desai: One more - how do you handle long-term storage of audit logs for compliance?
[08:49] Jordan Patel: Audit logs can be exported to your S3/GCS with lifecycle policies; retention configurable 90/180/365 days as part of the enterprise plan.
[08:58] Maya Chen: Ok jumping to quality monitoring - console ties evals to routing and will alert if a prompt set degrades. We can hook into your existing evaluation harness or use Redwood's eval suite.
[09:12] Liam O'Neill: If quality drops after quantization, can auto-roll back?
[09:16] Jordan Patel: Yes, rollback or route traffic back to the original variant automatically based on configured metric thresholds.
[09:24] [00:11:30] Maya Chen: Alright quick recap and recommended next steps. We'll run a POC benchmark: Redwood runs two quant profiles + baseline on a 10k prompt set, comparing cost and quality. We'll also send the pricing sheet and security pack.
[09:39] Samira Khan: Timeline wise we'd like to start POC within two weeks.
[09:44] Maya Chen: That works - we'll propose dates in the follow-up.
[09:48] Priya Desai: Can you also prepare a sample per-route dashboard with our tags?
[09:52] Jordan Patel: Yep we'll prepare a dashboard sample and a CSV mapping demo.
[09:57] [00:12:30] Liam O'Neill: Sounds good. one last competitor question - any differences if we were migrating from Anthropic stack?
[10:03] Jordan Patel: Mostly model conversion and tokenization quirks - we help with tokenizer mapping. Runtime differences exist but our goal is to preserve output parity.
[10:11] Maya Chen: Ok should we stop sharing?
[10:13] Samira Khan: Yup thanks everyone.
[10:15] [screen share ends]
[10:18] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with: pricing sheet, security pack, proposed POC dates, and the sample per-route dashboard CSV.
[10:26] Priya Desai: Thanks, look forward to it.
[10:29] Liam O'Neill: Thanks.
[10:31] Maya Chen: Bye.

Notes: occasional ASR errors - e.g., "CV cache" appears in transcript where speaker said "KV cache", timestamps approximate.
